# omx-dsp / fuzz_fx

omx-dsp's own fuzz target `fuzz_fx` ([source](source/fuzz_fx.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over omx-dsp 0.27.0 (FreeMixer/omx-dsp at a0ee1dfe).

Picks one of the 25 effect instance faces from the first byte, then a rate from the oracle grid or any rate from 8 to 768 kHz. It creates two instances at that rate. For up to eight steps it reads a bypass bit, the face's control ports as raw float or int words (NaN and infinities included), a block length of 1 to 512 frames and two channels of samples (finite at a chosen loudness, or any float word in hostile mode). Both instances get the same ports; one runs the block in place and the other out of place.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against libomxdsp.a, which build.sh compiles from omx-dsp's five src/*.c files with -DOMX_CONTRACTS and -ffp-contract=off as the library's Makefile does; the effect code is inline in the headers. The Makefile's own fuzz build uses native clang with libFuzzer, which this build replaces with the standard driver.
- omx-contract's headers are pinned to the tag v3.4.0 (1169c701), where the library's Makefile uses whichever omx-contract is installed, at or above its packaging floor of 3.1.0.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- Two inits of the same face at the same rate return the same answer ([lines 271-277](source/fuzz_fx.c#L271-L277)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- After init, after each resolve and after each run, no PRE, POST or invariant contract of the library is recorded as broken. Two tokens are skipped: rate-is-declared at a rate that is not declared, and bands-partition-unity. The ledger is not read in hostile mode ([lines 160-168](source/fuzz.h#L160-L168)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Running a block in place gives the same samples, bit for bit, as running it out of place on a twin instance that got the same ports ([lines 300-306](source/fuzz_fx.c#L300-L306)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- When init refused the rate, run() is the identity, bit for bit, whatever the ports say ([lines 307-314](source/fuzz_fx.c#L307-L314)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- An instance that accepted its rate and was given finite samples returns only finite samples, at any port value ([lines 315-323](source/fuzz_fx.c#L315-L323)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
